clue.text: Love fine voyage, naturally

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
a course is a route or passage a ship sails

explanation.surface: Someone who naturally adores a pleasant sea voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of agreement, meaning obviously or as anyone would expect.

clue.text: One yet to meet his match?

definitions.text: One yet to meet his match?

parts.words: One yet to meet his match?
parts.note: reads like a sportsman still unbeaten, but a match here is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: An undefeated champion awaiting a worthy opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man has not yet found the spouse he will wed, a match in the matrimonial sense.

clue.text: Small number, quiet at college feast

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
SH is the call for quiet
UP means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A few hushed students sitting down to a college banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: A NOSH-UP is British slang for a big, hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for a large, filling meal, which is what a feast is.

clue.text: Classy plane

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to shave a surface flat and even

explanation.surface: A stylish aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft but is the carpenter's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished in manner, and also the verb for levelling a surface, as a plane does to wood.

clue.text: Ineffectual type made out, coming into fortune

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come inside the word for fortune, as one comes into a room

parts.note: luck is fortune, good or bad

indicators.note: out describes the word made thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hapless fellow who was made out to be inheriting a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' reads as 'portrayed', but 'out' is the anagram signal and 'coming into' the container signal; a lame duck is also an official serving out a term after losing an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing that is weak and unable to cope, an idiom first used of failed stock traders.

clue.text: Immediately make amends, bagging century

indicators.note: bagging means pocketing, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to atone is to make amends
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Apologise straight away, even while scoring a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning without delay, straight away.

clue.text: Jumble taken from charitable event held in Portuguese resort

indicators.note: held in signals the charity event sits inside the resort's name

parts.note: Faro is a resort town on the Algarve coast of Portugal
a rag is a British student fundraising event for charity

explanation.surface: A muddle arising from a fundraiser on the Algarve.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused mixture or hotchpotch, the same as a jumble.

clue.text: Drink over money one lost in card game

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the drink above the rest

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: lost tells us the word one has gone missing from the word money

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gambling drink money away at cards, one stake lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes ONE out of MONEY, leaving MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game in which players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: Small company representative, put on

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
to put on is to feign, to act

explanation.surface: A minor firm's sales rep who is only pretending.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatly small and taking up little space.

clue.text: Copper, on lake trip abroad, finds criminal

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman on a holiday trip overseas tracks down a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element. 'abroad' turns TRIP into RIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The person responsible for a crime or wrongdoing, the guilty party.

clue.text: Vitality shown by The Bedroom Philosopher

indicators.note: shown by means displayed within the run of these words

explanation.surface: A comedy act called The Bedroom Philosopher shows plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bedroom Philosopher is an Australian comedy musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for energy, zest and attractive force.

clue.text: When childish tricks are played in college, one we wrecked

parts.note: a hall is a college or hall of residence at a university

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Students pulling pranks in college, one of them wrecking things.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening of 31 October, when children go trick-or-treating.

clue.text: Arts venue in Soho area, purely built to entertain Londoners, essentially?

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece holds the other
built means constructed afresh, so the letters are put together in a new order
essentially points to the core, the central letter of Londoners

explanation.surface: Asks whether a theatre in Soho was built purely to amuse the capital's residents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges SOHO AREA PURELY, and 'to entertain' takes in O, the middle letter of 'Londoners'.
explanation.definitionFit: The home of opera and ballet in Covent Garden, London, a leading venue for the performing arts.

clue.text: Almost board ship prior to travel ban

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to embark is to board a ship
the last letter dropped from the word for boarding a ship
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A travel ban imposed just before passengers can board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the K from EMBARK, giving EMBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban, especially on trade or shipping with a country.

clue.text: Prayer in book by Nobel Prize-winning author

parts.note: Doris Lessing won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2007

explanation.surface: A prayer found in a volume by a laureate writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short prayer asking for divine favour, such as grace before a meal.

clue.text: Plan revealed railway track

parts.note: out means made known, as a secret is out
a line is a railway track or route

explanation.surface: A rail scheme is unveiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough sketch or draft giving the main points, a plan.

clue.text: Become more involved in kitchen refurbishment

indicators.note: refurbishment means renovation, so the letters of kitchen are redone in another order

explanation.surface: Getting more deeply engaged in doing up a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of a plot that grows more complicated, as in 'the plot thickens'.

clue.text: A ride arranged on express? That's quite possible

indicators.note: arranged means set in order, so the letters are put in a different sequence

parts.note: to express is to say

explanation.surface: Booking a lift on an express train sounds plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversational phrase conceding something is probably true, much like 'perhaps so'.

clue.text: Short memo must be written about volunteers — every single one? Forget it

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a note is a memo
the final letter cut from the word for a memo

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the volunteers' abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
all means every single one

explanation.surface: A brief note must be sent to every volunteer, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts NOTE to NOT; 'about' turns TA into AT. The Territorial Army (TA) is Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal or denial, equivalent to telling someone to drop the matter.

clue.text: Master of talk broadcast, this teacher preps a king out of a sight

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order
out of says the king's letter is taken away from the scattered letters

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A broadcast about a teacher coaching a king's speech, as in the film about George VI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' and 'out of' together: the letters of THIS TEACHER PREPS are those of the answer plus R; 'a' and 'a sight' are padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who treats speech difficulties, so an expert in spoken language.

clue.text: Withdraw notice involving church close to Oxford

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: to see is to notice
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: close to means the end, the last letter of Oxford

explanation.surface: Leaving the church after a notice near Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like a written announcement, but here it is the verb, to spot; 'involving' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally break away from a federation or union, to withdraw.

clue.text: First in history, sitting in class, modest

indicators.note: sitting in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a caste is a social class

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the word history

explanation.surface: A modest student, top of the history class.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and virtuous in conduct, decent and restrained.

clue.text: Still considered almost odds-on, leader in Oaks?

parts.note: evens, one-to-one betting odds, sits just short of odds-on

indicators.note: leader in means the front letter of the word Oaks

explanation.surface: A racing tipster judging a favourite almost odds-on to win the Oaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a classic flat horse race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning nevertheless, in spite of that.

clue.text: Current duke was in charge, and did nothing

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
led means was in charge

explanation.surface: The present duke was in command and did nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazed about, past tense of the verb for spending time without doing anything.

clue.text: Ditch all the players on a team

parts.note: the cast is the full set of players in a production
taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Dropping the entire squad of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard or throw away something no longer wanted.

clue.text: Striking effect of chapter in contrary story

indicators.note: in places the chapter letter inside the turned word
contrary means going the opposite way, so the word for story is read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A chapter that makes a big impression in a story full of contradictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns TALE into ELAT, and 'in' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant success or conspicuous flair that creates a strong impression.

clue.text: Eating place row — better not to take sides

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise

indicators.note: taking no sides means dropping the outer letters of the word better

explanation.surface: A quarrel in a restaurant where it is wiser to stay neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dining area or room set aside for meals.

clue.text: Examine pulse, finding a skeleton in the cupboard?

parts.note: to scan is to examine
dal is a dish of lentils, and lentils are pulses

explanation.surface: A doctor checking a pulse and finding a skeleton hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is an edible seed such as a lentil.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton in the cupboard is a hidden disgrace that would shock if revealed.
